source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: ABB India's strategy is framed around 'local for local' manufacturing and 75 years of India-based production ('Make in India') serving 23 domestic market segments, not around China+1 sourcing diversification. Company is described as having 'a strong export presence, serving over 30 countries,' but this is not tied to a China-diversification narrative.

govt_capex.evidence: CY2024 order momentum attributed to 'the government's capital expenditure focus on new-age themes such as energy efficiency, decarbonization, and digitalization' and 'the government... aggressively pushing multiple targets of GDP growth, digital economy, exports, sustainability and clean energy through its infrastructure drive.' Key customer sectors cited include utilities, metals/mining, transport and energy -- segments with significant PSU/government linkage -- but no quantified % of revenue from government capex was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: PLI schemes are referenced as a macro/government demand driver for ABB India's customers and the broader economy, not as a benefit ABB India itself receives; no disclosure found of ABB India being a direct PLI scheme beneficiary.

china_plus_one.evidence: "China+1 Opportunity: With global companies derisking supply chains away from China, India is emerging as a strong alternative. Acutaas Chemicals is the first Indian company outside China to develop battery-grade electrolyte additives... enhances its leverage under the China+1 strategy." Also: "we have significantly reduced our dependence on Chinese imports, bringing China's share of raw material imports down from more than 70% to 21% by 2025, while increasing domestic and regional sourcing... India, which now accounts for 70% of imports."

rural.evidence: No rural revenue/market disclosure found; 'rural' only appears in CSR context (e.g., 'Rural Development - Supporting sustainable livelihoods... in rural communities'), not tied to product revenue.

govt_capex.evidence: No mention of government/infrastructure capex as a revenue driver found in MD&A or notes.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Standalone Notes, Exposure to Interest Rate Risk (as at March 31, 2025): 'Borrowing bearing fixed rate of interest - nil; Borrowing bearing variable rate of interest 634.90 lakhs; Total 634.90 lakhs' - effectively all borrowings are floating-rate (down sharply from Rs 20,272.97 lakhs total borrowings a year earlier, of which Rs 20,234.91 lakhs was variable-rate).

crude_exposure.evidence: No explicit crude-oil/petrochemical feedstock price linkage disclosed. Cost of materials consumed was Rs 56,684.02 lakhs on standalone revenue of Rs 98,333.91 lakhs (~57.6% of revenue) for FY25, but this is general raw-material cost, not specifically identified as crude-oil-linked.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Uses natural hedging plus foreign exchange forward contracts
inr_exposure.evidence: "The Company operates internationally and the major portion of business is transacted in USD & EURO... foreign exchange risk is catered by having natural hedge position for all receivables & Payables in USD. For other currencies, we are booking forward contract basis advice from consultants from time to time." Exports were 73.8-74% of revenue (mix of USD/EUR), but exact USD-only split not separately disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: No company-specific PLI participation disclosed. PLI mentioned only in generic industry-overview context (e.g., Bulk Drug Parks, semiconductor PLI schemes) as sector background, not as a benefit Acutaas itself receives.

china_plus_one.evidence: Backward integration into API manufacturing via Alkem Activa/Enzene noted in third-party coverage as reducing import dependency, but no explicit China+1/AR quote found

rural.evidence: Qualitative commentary on rural/semi-urban market penetration found in third-party sources; no revenue % disclosed

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Approximately 80% of forex exposure hedged per CFO commentary
inr_exposure.evidence: CFO commentary (earnings call coverage) indicating ~80% of forex exposure is hedged

pli_scheme.evidence: Supplier Kinvan identified as a PLI scheme beneficiary supplying Alkem; no evidence found that Alkem itself is a PLI scheme participant

china_plus_one.evidence: Company explicitly positions itself as a 'China-plus-one' CDMO alternative, stating it built its supply chain with minimal dependence on Chinese raw materials. CEO quoted: 'We're now the second source for many products made in China, and the first choice for new ones.' Growth is attributed to a 'China+1 reshoring wave' as multinational pharma diversify supply chains toward India, with cost arbitrage cited as a driver of Anthem's expansion (per IPO/DRHP-linked commentary).

crude_exposure.evidence: CDMO/specialty ingredients manufacturer using solvents and petrochemical-derived intermediates; no explicit crude-oil-linked exposure % disclosed in sources found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Described as an 'export-oriented business... susceptible to fluctuations in global logistics costs and raw material pricing,' serving 550+ clients across 44 countries including large pharma (AbbVie, Novartis, Pfizer). FY25 revenue Rs 1,844.55 crore (CRDMO segment 81.65%, Specialty Ingredients ~54.4% cross-tab). Explicit USD revenue % and hedging policy not found (AR PDF fetch blocked).

pli_scheme.evidence: Sector commentary notes the 2024 pharma PLI scheme and bulk-drug parks 'may help' Indian API/peptide manufacturers including Anthem ease production bottlenecks, but no disclosure found confirming Anthem is a current PLI scheme beneficiary.

china_plus_one.evidence: Bosch Group India President Guruprasad Mudlapur stated Bosch plans to double exports from India by 2030, leveraging India's cost-effective and competitive industrial base; framed as part of global automotive supply chains diversifying with India positioned to expand its export/manufacturing hub role (Business Standard interview, July 2025; Autocar Professional)

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company aims at reducing foreign exchange risks by hedging its net exposures, with investments and hedging carried out per clearly defined internal guidelines specifying processes and responsibilities
inr_exposure.evidence: "Investments and hedging are carried out as per clearly defined internal guidelines specifying processes and responsibilities. The Company aims at reducing foreign exchange risks by hedging its net exposures and constantly monitoring the risks." (paraphrase of Bosch Ltd Directors' Report, via India Infoline)

pli_scheme.evidence: Bosch was among 75 companies that secured approval under India's Component Champion Incentive Scheme (part of the Auto PLI scheme) on March 15, 2022

china_plus_one.evidence: Management describes import substitution as 'the single biggest opportunity for Data Patterns,' with strategy 'built on replacing imports with Indian-designed systems' amid India's Atmanirbhar Bharat defence indigenisation push (India's defence import dependency fell from 62% in FY02 to 12% in FY25). Framed as broad import/foreign-supplier substitution (radar, EW, avionics) rather than specifically anti-China.

govt_capex.evidence: Customer base is almost entirely government/public-sector entities with no single private customer; major customers include Ministry of Defence, DRDO, BrahMos Aerospace, Bharat Electronics Ltd, BHEL, HAL, ECIL and ISRO units. FY25 order book was ₹730 crore (incl. ~₹53 crore export order book) on revenue of ₹755 crore, implying government/defence exposure approaches the totality of revenue, though no exact % was found disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: No disclosure found of Data Patterns participating in a PLI scheme; a dedicated PLI scheme for defence electronics does not appear to currently exist in India (industry bodies have only recommended one) as of sources checked.

china_plus_one.evidence: Chairman & MD's statement in the FY2024-25 Annual Report: 'The China+1 strategy and global supply chain diversification efforts are further enhancing India's role as a trusted global manufacturing hub.' The AR also positions India as an emerging preferred destination for peptide API and CDMO manufacturing given capacity constraints in the US/EU/China, but no explicit sentence was found directly attributing Divi's own revenue/order growth to China+1 dynamics, so this is scored 'moderate' rather than 'strong'.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue (~88% of sales, largely to Europe and North America) implies substantial USD/EUR exposure, but the specific USD revenue percentage and forward-contract hedging policy could not be verified directly against the financial risk management notes in the AR.

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's Laboratories (Bollaram and Visakhapatnam API campuses) is identified in industry/government coverage as part of the pool of ~55 qualified companies under the Government of India's PLI scheme for bulk drugs/APIs/KSMs (Category 2, ~Rs 6,940-15,000 crore outlay across sources, FY2022-23 to FY2028-29); exact incentive amount received by Divi's specifically was not found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Royal Enfield's exports grew sharply in FY25 (unit exports up ~30% YoY to 100,136 motorcycles out of 1,002,893 total; management cites expansion across 60+ countries, North America, Latin America, Asia-Pacific and Europe, and a #1 position in SAARC markets). No explicit 'China+1'/supply-chain-diversification framing was found attributing this growth to customers shifting away from China; separately, Eicher has had to adapt sourcing due to China's export curbs on rare-earth magnets, i.e. China risk runs against Eicher here rather than in its favor.

rural.evidence: Analyst commentary on VECV (commercial vehicles JV) notes growth 'driven by replacement demand, rural consumption, and infrastructure development' and that new Eicher Pro truck models 'gained significant traction in both urban and rural markets' in FY25 (third-party summary, not a direct AR quote).

govt_capex.evidence: Third-party FY25 commentary on VECV states 'the government doubles down on rural connectivity and highway development,' framing government infrastructure spend as a demand driver for commercial trucks (not a direct AR quote; primary MD&A text could not be accessed).

pli_scheme.evidence: India's PLI scheme for autos/auto-components could plausibly apply to VECV's auto-components business and to EV localization; one third-party estimate speculates INR 200-600 crore of potential incentives over the scheme period, but no confirmed disclosure of actual Eicher/VECV PLI participation or benefit was found in accessible sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: No China+1/supply-chain-diversification narrative attributed to Emcure specifically was found. General industry commentary frames 'China Plus One' as a tailwind for the Indian API/pharma industry broadly, and Emcure has an in-house API vertical (ARV, oncology, cardiovascular APIs), but this is third-party industry framing, not a company-specific statement in Emcure's own reporting.

rural.evidence: Only reference found is CSR-related rural outreach (education, preventive healthcare community programs), which is a CSR spend category, not a sales/revenue metric.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Total debt (incl. lease liabilities) fell from ~Rs 2,320 cr (Mar-24) to ~Rs 1,022 cr (Mar-25) after ~Rs 600 cr of July-2024 IPO proceeds were used to prepay term loans; gearing improved from 1.03x to 0.27x. No explicit floating-vs-fixed-rate borrowing split was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: International revenue (Emerging Markets + Europe + Canada) was ~53.65% of FY2024-25 consolidated revenue, spanning multiple currencies; not confirmed as USD-specific, and no explicit hedging policy disclosure was verified against primary financial risk management notes.

pli_scheme.evidence: Emcure has an in-house API manufacturing vertical (e.g. Atazanavir, Dolutegravir, Tenofovir) that is plausibly eligible under India's PLI scheme for APIs/KSMs, but no disclosure confirming actual scheme participation or benefit was found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company held a net cash position of ~Rs 107 crore as of March 31, 2024 (cash & equivalents incl. mutual funds of Rs 464 crore vs Rs 282 crore prior year), indicating low reliance on debt; floating-rate liability % not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Formulations manufacturer; API/excipient raw material cost structure not detailed with crude-oil linkage in sources found.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY24 total revenue ~Rs 3,918 crore: domestic formulations ~Rs 2,269 crore (58%), international formulations ~Rs 1,649 crore (42%), exporting to 40+ countries. Company operates in Russia via a wholly-owned subsidiary and in Ukraine/CIS via distributors, with Russia and South Africa described as 'other home markets.' Explicit hedging policy and USD-specific % not found (AR PDF fetch blocked).

pli_scheme.evidence: No disclosure found confirming JB Pharma as a beneficiary of the pharma PLI scheme for APIs/KSMs/drug intermediates.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Layered hedging strategy combining natural hedges and forex derivatives
inr_exposure.evidence: Lupin operates in 100+ markets and is exposed to currency fluctuations, particularly USD-INR, EUR-INR, and ZAR-INR; natural hedges and forex derivatives are deployed, with treasury operations monitoring exposures and adopting layered hedging strategies (per Lupin Enterprise Risk Management Policy).

pli_scheme.evidence: Lupin is a major API/bulk drug manufacturer operating in the same space targeted by India's PLI Scheme for Bulk Drugs (Rs 6,940 crore incentive covering 41 API/KSM products), but no source confirms Lupin as a named PLI beneficiary or discloses PLI-linked revenue/capex.

inr_exposure.evidence: Search-engine summary of Global Health Ltd's FY2024-25 BRSR filing (via NSE) states: 'deemed export of services was 5.19% of total turnover in FY 2024-25' - deemed exports typically denote foreign-exchange-earning revenue from international/foreign national patients treated in India; currency composition not specified in the snippet.

rural.evidence: Third-party FY25 coverage notes distribution expansion into rural and smaller towns and double-digit growth from domestic subsidiaries in recent quarters, but no revenue % was disclosed in accessible sources

crude_exposure.evidence: VAM (vinyl acetate monomer) described as a key raw material input with multiple sourcing arrangements to ensure supply continuity; crude-linked input fluctuations noted as a margin driver (FY25 EBITDA margin 23.6% vs 22.9% prior year), but no raw-material-cost % was disclosed in accessible sources

rural.evidence: Company's pan-India distribution network reaches over 60,000 retail outlets with stated emphasis on semi-urban and rural penetration as part of its growth strategy; no quantified rural revenue % disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company is targeting a net debt-free status by H1 FY27 and reduced net debt by ~Rs 329 crore in FY26, indicating declining leverage; floating-rate liability % not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are ENA (linked to grain prices), glass and packaging; ENA costs rose on high grain prices while glass/packaging costs eased in recent periods. No explicit crude-oil-linked exposure quantified.

inr_exposure.evidence: Radico derives ~5-6% of sales volumes and ~9-10% of revenue from exports to over 100 countries, with key markets including the US, Canada, Europe and Southeast Asia. No hedging policy details found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Not applicable — no PLI scheme relevant to the alcobev sector.

govt_capex.evidence: Search-derived paraphrase (not a direct AR quote): infrastructure-driven TMT demand cited as a growth opportunity; India's steel sector benefits from sustained infrastructure spending and urbanization, with domestic demand growing an estimated 7-8% annually. No specific revenue percentage tied to government projects was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Search snippet: 'Exports comprised ~10% in FY25, providing some cushion against domestic demand cycles' - implies some USD-denominated revenue but not explicitly confirmed as USD-denominated, and no hedging policy was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: General industry context only: Government of India's Rs 6,322 crore PLI scheme for specialty steel (approved July 2021, covering FY24-FY28). No source found confirming Shyam Metalics as a named beneficiary/allottee.

china_plus_one.evidence: AR/investor materials describe supply-chain de-risking after China restricted heavy rare-earth magnet exports — Sona shifted to alternative motor designs using light rare-earth or no heavy rare-earth magnets to keep supplying EV 2W/3W motors. Company is simultaneously entering China's EV market via a ~$20mn JV with Jinnaite Machinery (JNT) as part of a 'look-east' strategy, and diversifying into non-auto (e.g., acquiring Escorts Kubota's Railway Equipment Division). EV order book stood at Rs 235bn (Q3 FY26) with EV programs at 71% of orders, reflecting global OEM diversification of supplier base — a moderate rather than explicit 'AR attributes revenue growth directly to China+1' framing.

crude_exposure.evidence: Auto component manufacturer using steel, aluminum and rare-earth magnets as key inputs; no crude-oil-linked raw material exposure disclosed in sources found.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue mix by geography: North America 28%, India 40%, Europe 26%, Asia 5%, Rest of World 1% (on FY25 revenue of ~Rs 3,555 crore), implying ~60% international/export revenue. Explicit USD-hedging policy and USD-specific revenue % not found (AR PDF fetch blocked).

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona Comstar was the first Indian auto-component supplier to receive Auto PLI certification (hub-wheel-drive motor for e-two-wheelers), and received PLI certification for three additional EV traction motors (2x e-three-wheeler, 1x e-two-wheeler) in August 2025. Revenue contribution from PLI-certified products not separately disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Sun Pharma API Business leadership described continuing supply chain resilience by working with indigenous (domestic) sources and improving forecasting vs. inventory during supply disruptions (paraphrase from third-party industry coverage, not verified against AR text directly)

rural.evidence: India sales growth attributed in part to broader coverage in semi-urban and rural areas (paraphrase from earnings-period press coverage); no percentage disclosed

china_plus_one.evidence: No China+1/supply-chain-diversification narrative found. Titan's international jewellery/watch business (including CaratLane international, UAE, North America, ~32 export countries) is framed as organic international expansion, not a China+1 beneficiary story.

rural.evidence: Titan's FY25 growth strategy is described as 'targeting both value and premium segments across urban and expanding rural India,' with continued investment in Tier 3-4 store rollouts (network grew to 3,100+ stores across 600+ cities); no quantified rural revenue percentage was found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: A CARE Ratings note (Sept 2025) indicates FY25 short-term borrowings rose, driven by Gold Metal Loans (up >46% YoY), commercial paper, and working-capital loans used to fund gold procurement amid rising gold prices; net TOL/TNW rose to 2.2x (Mar-25) from 2.0x (Mar-24). No explicit floating-vs-fixed-rate percentage split was disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Third-party analyst commentary (not a confirmed direct AR quote) describes Titan as running a near-full/high gold-price and currency hedging program to protect margins against gold-price and USD-INR volatility on its import-dependent gold procurement, said to be among the highest hedging ratios in the industry versus partially-hedged or unhedged peers.
inr_exposure.evidence: Secondary source paraphrase: 'Titan Company follows a high/near-100% gold hedging strategy... which protects it from volatility in gold prices... many peers... do not hedge or only partially hedge.' Not verified against Titan's own financial risk management notes.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI (Production Linked Incentive) scheme participation found; jewellery/watches/eyewear retail is not a PLI-covered sector for Titan.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue break-up (FundsIndia equity research summary): India 55%, Brazil 10%, US 10%, Germany 10%, Other markets 15%. Implies material non-INR revenue (USD, EUR, BRL) but no explicit hedging policy text was accessible.

crude_exposure.evidence: Industry raw material costs are primarily driven by ENA (extra neutral alcohol), grain, and glass packaging, not directly crude-oil-linked; no explicit crude oil exposure disclosed in sources found.

inr_exposure.evidence: USL is described as a primarily domestic-revenue business with exports of certain brands to 30+ countries and participation in global travel retail; no quantified USD revenue % or hedging policy found. FY24 revenue from operations was ~Rs 26,018 crore, overwhelmingly domestic.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme relevant to the alcobev sector; not applicable.
